parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish ácana, probably from Ciboney languages or Taíno.

parole.significato: sweet potato (plant)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish batata, from Taíno batata. Doublet of potato.

parole.significato: hut (a small timber dwelling with thatched roof)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish bohío, Taíno *bohi (“house, dwelling”) (compare Lokono bohy (“house”)). From the Taíno term used by the natives of Hispaniola and other Caribbean islands, as recorded by Spanish colonizers.

parole.significato: A Cuban type of sweet potato with light-colored flesh that is drier and less sweet than the varieties typical in the US…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish boniato (“sweet potato”).

parole.significato: A tribal chief in the Spanish West Indies.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish cacique, from Taíno *kasike or Lokono kassequa, cazaqah (“chieftain; power”).

parole.significato: A small long and narrow boat, propelled by one or more people (depending on the size of canoe), using single-bladed pad…
parole.testo: Adopted in 16th century from Spanish canoa, from Taíno *kanowa (“dugout canoe”) (compare Lokono kanoa (“canoe”), Wayuu anuwa, anua (“boat, canoe”)), from Proto-Arawak *kanawa.

parole.significato: Manioc (Manihot esculenta), a tropical plant which is the source of tapioca.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish cazabe, from Taíno *kasabi (“cassava flour”) (whence Garifuna sibiba), from Proto-Arawak *sapi.

parole.significato: A small, low island largely made of sand or coral.
parole.testo: ] From Spanish cayo, from Taíno.

parole.significato: A small island or ledge of rock in the water; a key.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish cayo, from Taíno cayo (“small island”). Doublet of key.

parole.significato: Any tree of the genus Ceiba, the best-known of which is Ceiba pentandra.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish ceiba.

parole.significato: Any of a number of species of bioluminescent beetle in the Pyrophorus genus
parole.testo: From Spanish cocuyo. From Taíno kokuyo.

parole.significato: The soursop or custard apple.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish guanábana, from Taíno.

parole.significato: red-tailed hawk (Buteo jamaicensis)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish guaraguao.

parole.significato: A tropical tree or shrub of the myrtle family, Psidium guajava.
parole.testo: Recorded since 1555, from Spanish guayaba, from Taíno *wayaba. Doublet of guayaba, which is now rare or obsolete.

parole.significato: The guava (tree or fruit).
parole.testo: From Spanish guayaba, from Taíno *wayaba. Doublet of guava, by which it has been largely displaced.

parole.significato: Any of various trees of Latin America which typically have strong, hard wood.
parole.testo: From Spanish guayacán, from Taíno waiacan.

parole.significato: Synonym of sekere.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish güiro.

parole.significato: A swinging couch or bed, usually made of netting or canvas about six feet (1.8 meters) wide, suspended by clews or cord…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish hamaca, from Taíno *hamaka (compare Lokono hamaka, Wayuu jama'a), from Proto-Arawak *maka. parole.significato: A type of large cigar produced in Cuba.
parole.testo: From Spanish La Habana, from Habaguanex, the native American chief (cacique) who controlled the area, the name derived from Taíno sabana (“savannah”). The letter h may be an anthroponymic inflection.

parole.significato: A tropical American agave, Agave fourcroydes, whose thick, sword-shaped leaves yield a coarse reddish fibre used in mak…
parole.testo: From Spanish henequén, probably of Taíno origin.

parole.significato: A severe tropical cyclone; an intense storm rotating around a central eye.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish huracán, ultimately from Taíno *hurakā.

parole.significato: Any of the medium-sized rodents of the subfamily Capromyinae, which inhabit the Caribbean islands.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish jutía.

parole.significato: A green iguana (Iguana iguana), a large tropical American lizard often kept as a pet.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish iguana, from Taíno *iwana.

parole.significato: One of a string of small islands.
parole.testo: Variant of cay, from Spanish cayo, from Taíno cayo (“small island”)

parole.significato: Any of various large agaves of Mexico and the southern US, especially the American aloe, Agave americana.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish maguey, from Taíno *mawei.

parole.significato: Corn; a type of grain of the species Zea mays.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish maíz, from Taíno *mahis, *mahisi, from Proto-Arawak *marikɨ. Cognate with Lokono marisi, Wayuu maiki.

parole.significato: An evergreen tree of species Mammea americana, or its edible fruit.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish mamey, from Taíno.

parole.significato: A tropical flea, the chigoe.
parole.testo: From Spanish nigua, from Taíno [Term?].

parole.significato: The edible starchy tuber of the plant species Solanum tuberosum.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish patata, itself borrowed from Taíno batata (“sweet potato”). Doublet of batata.

parole.significato: A mixed woodland-grassland biome and ecosystem characterised by the trees being sufficiently widely spaced so that the…
parole.testo: From Spanish sabana, from Taíno.

parole.significato: Either of two large evergreens of the West Indies, Podocarpus coriaceus and Podocarpus purdieanus.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish yaca, from Taíno.

parole.significato: cassava
parole.testo: Via Spanish yuca (also historically juca), frequently said to be of Taíno origin. While the word is almost certainly from an indigenous American language, the source is not known. Perhaps from Kari'na yuca (“cassava”) , but this appears to be a ghost word. Doublet of yucca.
